hook.convey: a ruler measures length as the number of 1 cm spaces from one end to the other; start at 0 and the end mark is the length; start anywhere else and take the start mark away from the end mark

use.hi: Drawing mein tum scale se seedhi line kheenchte ho. Aaj usi scale se cheezein naapna seekhenge: kahan se shuru karein aur lambai kaise padhein.
use.en: In drawing you use a ruler to draw straight lines. Today we learn to measure things with that same ruler: where to start and how to read the length.

use.hi: Cricket bat ka grip kitna lamba hai, yeh scale se naap sakte hain. Agar scale ka shuru wala hissa toota ho, tab bhi sahi lambai nikal sakti hai.
use.en: We can measure how long a cricket bat's grip is with a ruler. Even if the start of the ruler is broken, we can still find the right length.

explain.convey: pencil from the 0 mark to the 7 mark → 7 spaces of 1 cm → 7 cm; from 0 the end mark is the length

point.hi: Dekho, pencil scale ke 0 se shuru hoti hai aur 7 pe khatam hoti hai. Toh pencil 7 cm lambi hai. 0 se shuru karo, toh aakhri nishaan hi lambai batata hai.
point.en: Look, the pencil starts at 0 on the ruler and ends at 7. So the pencil is 7 cm long. Start at 0, and the end mark tells the length.

prompt.hi: Ab doosri pencil scale pe 2 ke nishaan se 8 ke nishaan tak rakhi hai. Kya yeh pencil 8 cm lambi hai, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: Now another pencil lies on the ruler from the 2 mark to the 8 mark. Is this pencil 8 cm long, yes or no?

why.hi: pehli pencil 0 se 7 tak thi, doosri 2 se 8 tak hai, toh 8 − 2 = 6 cm
why.en: the first pencil went 0 to 7; the second goes 2 to 8, so 8 − 2 = 6 cm

simpler.hi: Lambai shuru ke nishaan se ginte hain, sirf aakhri nishaan se nahi. Yeh pencil 2 se shuru hoti hai, 0 se nahi.
simpler.en: Length is counted from the starting mark, not just read at the end mark. This pencil starts at 2, not at 0.

explain.convey: crayon from the 3 mark to the 9 mark → count the 1 cm spaces, not the marks → 6 spaces → 9 − 3 = 6 → 6 cm, not 9 cm

point.hi: Yeh crayon scale pe 3 se shuru hota hai aur 9 pe khatam. Nishaan nahi, khaane gino: 3 se 9 tak 1-1 cm ke 6 khaane hain, yaani 9 − 3 = 6. Toh crayon 6 cm lamba hai, 9 cm nahi.
point.en: This crayon starts at 3 on the ruler and ends at 9. Count the spaces, not the marks: from 3 to 9 there are 6 spaces of 1 cm, that is 9 − 3 = 6. So the crayon is 6 cm long, not 9 cm.

prompt.hi: Ab ek doosra crayon scale pe 5 ke nishaan se 12 ke nishaan tak hai. Yeh crayon kitna lamba hai?
prompt.en: Now another crayon lies on the ruler from the 5 mark to the 12 mark. How long is this crayon?

why.hi: crayon 3 se 9 tak 6 cm tha; doosra 5 se 12 tak hai, toh 12 − 5 = 7 khaane
why.en: the crayon went 3 to 9, 6 cm; the second goes 5 to 12, so 12 − 5 = 7 spaces

simpler.hi: Nishaan nahi, beech ke khaane gino. 5 se 12 tak har cm ka khaana gino, ya 12 mein se 5 ghatao.
simpler.en: Count the spaces, not the marks. Count each cm space from 5 to 12, or take 5 away from 12.

explain.convey: starting at 1 instead of 0: object from 1 to 6 covers 5 spaces, not 6 → reading the end mark from 1 gives 1 cm too much

point.hi: Agar pencil 1 ke nishaan se shuru ho aur 6 pe khatam, toh beech mein sirf 5 khaane hain, 6 nahi. 1 se shuru karke sirf aakhri nishaan padhoge, toh lambai 1 cm zyada aayegi.
point.en: If a pencil starts at the 1 mark and ends at 6, there are only 5 spaces in between, not 6. If you start at 1 and read only the end mark, the length comes out 1 cm too much.

prompt.hi: {friend} ne ek patta scale ke 1 ke nishaan se 9 ke nishaan tak rakha aur lambai 9 cm likhi. Patte ki sahi lambai kitni hai?
prompt.en: {friend} placed a leaf from the 1 mark to the 9 mark on a ruler and wrote the length as 9 cm. What is the leaf's correct length?

why.hi: pencil 1 se 6 tak 5 khaane thi; patta 1 se 9 tak hai, toh 9 − 1 = 8 khaane
why.en: the pencil went 1 to 6, 5 spaces; the leaf goes 1 to 9, so 9 − 1 = 8 spaces

simpler.hi: 1 se shuru karne par aakhri nishaan lambai 1 cm zyada bata deta hai. Toh 9 mein se 1 ghatao.
simpler.en: Starting at 1, the end mark gives a length 1 cm too much. So take 1 away from 9.

problem.hi: Ek lakdi scale pe 2 ke nishaan se 11 ke nishaan tak rakhi hai. Lakdi kitni lambi hai?
problem.en: A stick lies on a ruler from the 2 mark to the 11 mark. How long is the stick?

simpler.hi: Lakdi 2 se shuru hoti hai, 0 se nahi. 2 se 11 tak kitne cm hain, yeh gino.
simpler.en: The stick starts at 2, not at 0. Count the cm from 2 to 11.

givens.hi: lakdi ka shuru 2 ke nishaan pe hai
givens.en: the stick starts at the 2 mark

givens.hi: lakdi ka aakhri sira 11 ke nishaan pe hai
givens.en: the stick ends at the 11 mark

find.en: the length of the stick, in cm

do.hi: Pehle dekho lakdi kahan se shuru hoti hai
do.en: First see where the stick starts

why.hi: 0 se shuru na ho toh sirf aakhri nishaan lambai nahi batata
why.en: when it does not start at 0, the end mark alone does not give the length

simpler.hi: Stick 2 ke nishaan se shuru hoti hai, 0 se nahi. Isliye sirf aakhri nishaan 11 padhne se lambai nahi milegi.
simpler.en: The stick starts at the 2 mark, not at 0. So just reading the end mark 11 will not give the length.

do.hi: Ab tay karo ki kya karna hai

steps.result: aakhri nishaan 11 mein se shuru ka nishaan 2 ghatana hai

why.hi: ghatane se 2 se 11 tak ke 1-1 cm ke khaane gine jaate hain
why.en: taking away counts the 1 cm spaces from 2 to 11

simpler.hi: Lambai ke liye 11 mein se 2 ghatao. Isse 2 se 11 tak ke saare cm khaane gine jaate hain.
simpler.en: For the length, take 2 away from 11. This counts all the cm spaces from 2 to 11.

prompt.hi: Ab 11 mein se 2 ghatao. Lakdi kitni lambi hai?
prompt.en: Now take 2 away from 11. How long is the stick?

simpler.hi: 2 se 11 tak aage gino, har kadam ek cm hai. Jitne kadam lage, utne cm lambi stick hai.
simpler.en: Count on from 2 to 11; each step is one cm. The stick is as many cm long as the steps you took.

why.hi: lakdi ka shuru 2 pe aur aakhri sira 11 pe hai, toh lambai 11 − 2 = 9 cm hai
why.en: the stick starts at 2 and ends at 11, so its length is 11 − 2 = 9 cm

why.hi: lakdi ka shuru 2 pe aur aakhri sira 11 pe hai, toh lambai 11 − 2 = 9 cm hai
why.en: the stick starts at 2 and ends at 11, so its length is 11 − 2 = 9 cm

prompt.hi: Ek rubber scale pe 4 ke nishaan se 10 ke nishaan tak rakha hai. Rubber ki lambai cm mein batao.
prompt.en: An eraser lies on a ruler from the 4 mark to the 10 mark. Give the eraser's length in cm.

why.hi: rubber 4 ke nishaan se 10 ke nishaan tak hai, toh lambai 10 − 4 = 6 cm hai
why.en: the eraser goes from the 4 mark to the 10 mark, so its length is 10 − 4 = 6 cm

simpler.hi: Rubber 4 ke nishaan se shuru hota hai. Toh 10 mein se 4 ghatao, ya 4 se 10 tak ke khaane gino.
simpler.en: The eraser starts at the 4 mark. So take 4 away from 10, or count the spaces from 4 to 10.

prompt.hi: Laal crayon scale pe 0 se 8 ke nishaan tak hai. Neela crayon 3 se 10 ke nishaan tak hai. Kaunsa lamba hai, laal ya neela?
prompt.en: The red crayon lies on a ruler from 0 to the 8 mark. The blue crayon lies from 3 to the 10 mark. Which is longer, red or blue?

why.hi: laal 0 se 8 tak hai, yaani 8 cm, aur neela 3 se 10 tak, yaani 10 − 3 = 7 cm
why.en: red goes 0 to 8, that is 8 cm; blue goes 3 to 10, so 10 − 3 = 7 cm

simpler.hi: Dono ki lambai alag-alag nikalo: aakhri nishaan mein se shuru ka nishaan ghatao. Neela 3 se shuru hota hai, 0 se nahi.
simpler.en: Find each length separately: take the starting mark away from the end mark. Blue starts at 3, not at 0.

ladder.why: warm-up: object from 0 → the end mark is the length
same idea on a real object, an ID card from the 0 cm mark
predict for a crayon from 3 to 9 → 6 cm, not the end mark 9
say why: length counts the 1 cm spaces, so starting at 1 gives 1 cm too much

remediation.move: broken ruler that starts at 4, a key from 4 to 9 with each 1 cm space shown as one hop → length is the spaces, not the marks → check by end mark − start mark

say.hi: Lambai khaane ginkar nikalti hai, nishaan ginkar nahi. 4 se 9 tak 1-1 cm ke 5 khaane hain, aur 9 − 4 = 5 bhi hai.
say.en: Length comes from counting the spaces, not the marks. From 4 to 9 there are 5 spaces of 1 cm, and 9 − 4 = 5 too.

simpler.hi: Khaane gino, nishaan nahi. 4 se 9 tak 1 cm ke 5 khaane hain, toh lambai 5 cm hai.
simpler.en: Count the spaces, not the marks. From 4 to 9 there are 5 spaces of 1 cm, so the length is 5 cm.

prompt.hi: Toote scale pe ek chabi 6 ke nishaan se 13 ke nishaan tak hai. Chabi kitni lambi hai?
prompt.en: On a broken ruler a key lies from the 6 mark to the 13 mark. How long is the key?

why.hi: chabi 6 ke nishaan se 13 ke nishaan tak hai, toh lambai 13 − 6 = 7 cm hai
why.en: the key goes from the 6 mark to the 13 mark, so its length is 13 − 6 = 7 cm

simpler.hi: Chabi 6 ke nishaan se shuru hoti hai. Toh 13 mein se 6 ghatao, ya 6 se 13 tak ke khaane gino.
simpler.en: The key starts at the 6 mark. So take 6 away from 13, or count the spaces from 6 to 13.

bridgeToNext.hi: Chhoti cheezein hum cm mein naapte hain. Par rassi ya kamra bahut lamba hota hai, uske liye metre hai. Ab dekhenge ki 1 metre mein kitne cm hote hain.
bridgeToNext.en: We measure small things in cm. But a rope or a room is very long, and for that there is the metre. Next we see how many cm make 1 metre.

simpler.hi: Chhoti cheezein hum cm mein naapte hain. Lambi cheezon ke liye metre hota hai. Agle hisse mein dekhenge ki 1 metre mein kitne cm hote hain.
simpler.en: We measure small things in cm. Long things are measured in metres. Next we see how many cm are in 1 metre.

hook.convey: long things are measured in metres, and 1 m = 100 cm; m → cm: each metre is 100 cm, then add the extra cm; cm → m and cm: every 100 cm is 1 m, the rest stays cm

use.hi: Football ke goal ke saamne line banane ke liye rassi chahiye. Rassi metre mein milti hai, par dukaan wala tape se cm mein naapta hai. Dono ka rishta aaj samjhenge.
use.en: To mark a line in front of the football goal we need a rope. The rope is sold in metres, but the shopkeeper measures in cm with a tape. Today we understand how the two are linked.

use.hi: Rangoli ki drawing ke border ke liye ribbon lagana hai. Kuch ribbon m mein likhe hain aur kuch cm mein. Jodne se pehle sab ko ek hi ikai mein badalna seekhenge.
use.en: We want ribbon for the border of a rangoli drawing. Some ribbons are written in m and some in cm. We will learn to change them all to one unit before adding.

explain.convey: a metre scale has 100 spaces of 1 cm → 1 m = 100 cm; 10 cm is only a short piece of a metre, not a metre

point.hi: Metre scale pe 1-1 cm ke 100 khaane hote hain, toh 1 m = 100 cm. 10 cm toh metre ka bas ek chhota tukda hai, 10 cm metre nahi hai.
point.en: A metre scale has 100 spaces of 1 cm each, so 1 m = 100 cm. 10 cm is just a short piece of a metre; 10 cm is not a metre.

prompt.hi: Ek rassi 3 metre scale jitni lambi hai, yaani 3 m. Rassi kitne cm lambi hai?
prompt.en: A rope is as long as 3 metre scales, that is 3 m. How many cm long is the rope?

why.hi: 1 metre mein 100 khaane yaani 100 cm hain, toh rassi ke 3 m = 300 cm
why.en: 1 metre has 100 spaces, that is 100 cm, so the rope's 3 m = 300 cm

simpler.hi: 1 m mein 100 cm hote hain. Rassi 3 m hai, toh 100 cm teen baar jodo.
simpler.en: 1 m has 100 cm. The rope is 3 m, so add 100 cm three times.

explain.convey: 2 m 8 cm → metres first: 2 m = 200 cm → add 8 → 208 cm; the metres fill the hundreds place, so it is never 28

mustSay.en: change the metres to cm first

point.hi: 2 m 8 cm mein pehle metre ko cm banao: 2 m = 200 cm. Phir 8 cm jodo: 200 + 8 = 208. Yaad rakho, 2 metre sau ki jagah par aate hain, isliye 2 m 8 cm = 208 cm, 28 cm nahi.
point.en: In 2 m 8 cm, change the metres to cm first: 2 m = 200 cm. Then add 8 cm: 200 + 8 = 208. Remember, the 2 metres go in the hundreds place, so 2 m 8 cm = 208 cm, not 28 cm.

prompt.hi: Ek ribbon 3 m 6 cm lamba hai. Isi tarah socho: ribbon kitne cm lamba hai?
prompt.en: A ribbon is 3 m 6 cm long. Thinking the same way, how many cm long is the ribbon?

why.hi: 1 m = 100 cm, toh ribbon ke 3 m = 300 cm, aur 300 + 6 = 306
why.en: 1 m = 100 cm, so the ribbon's 3 m = 300 cm, and 300 + 6 = 306

simpler.hi: Pehle 3 m ko cm mein badlo, jaise 2 m 200 cm bana tha. Phir usmein 6 cm jodo.
simpler.en: First change 3 m to cm, just as 2 m became 200 cm. Then add 6 cm to it.

explain.convey: 250 cm → take out each full 100 cm as 1 m → 200 cm = 2 m, 50 cm left → 2 m 50 cm

point.hi: Ulta bhi kar sakte hain. 250 cm mein 200 cm hain, aur har 100 cm = 1 m, toh 200 cm = 2 m. Bache 50 cm. Toh 250 cm = 2 m 50 cm.
point.en: We can go the other way too. 250 cm has 200 cm in it, and every 100 cm = 1 m, so 200 cm = 2 m. 50 cm are left. So 250 cm = 2 m 50 cm.

prompt.hi: Ek kapda 460 cm lamba hai. Uski lambai metre aur cm mein batao.
prompt.en: A cloth is 460 cm long. Give its length in metres and centimetres.

why.hi: kapda 460 cm hai; har 100 cm = 1 m, toh 4 poore metre aur 60 cm bachte hain
why.en: the cloth is 460 cm; each 100 cm = 1 m, so 4 full metres and 60 cm are left

simpler.hi: 460 cm mein har 100 cm ek metre banata hai. Dekho kitne poore 100 hain, aur kitne cm bachte hain.
simpler.en: In 460 cm, every 100 cm makes one metre. See how many full 100s there are, and how many cm are left.

problem.hi: {friend} ke paas patang ki 6 m 25 cm dor hai. Usme se 75 cm dor patang baandhne mein lag gayi. Yaad rakho, 1 m = 100 cm. Kitni dor bachi? Jawab metre aur cm mein do.
problem.en: {friend} has 6 m 25 cm of kite string. 75 cm of it is used to tie the kite. Remember, 1 m = 100 cm. How much string is left? Give the answer in metres and centimetres.

simpler.hi: Pehle 6 m 25 cm ko sirf cm mein badlo. Phir usme se 75 cm ghatao.
simpler.en: First change 6 m 25 cm into cm only. Then take 75 cm away from it.

givens.hi: 75 cm dor patang mein lag gayi

find.hi: bachi hui dor, metre aur cm mein
find.en: the string left, in m and cm

do.hi: Pehle 6 m 25 cm ko cm mein badlo
do.en: First change 6 m 25 cm to cm

why.hi: 1 m = 100 cm hai, toh 6 m = 600 cm
why.en: 1 m = 100 cm, so 6 m = 600 cm

simpler.hi: 1 m = 100 cm, toh 6 m = 600 cm. Usmein 25 cm jodo, toh 625 cm bane.
simpler.en: 1 m = 100 cm, so 6 m = 600 cm. Add 25 cm to it to make 625 cm.

do.en: Now take away the string used

why.hi: ghatane se pehle dono lambai ek hi ikai cm mein honi chahiye
why.en: both lengths must be in the same unit, cm, before taking away

simpler.hi: Ab dono lambai cm mein hain. 625 cm mein se 75 cm ghatao, 550 cm bache.
simpler.en: Now both lengths are in cm. Take 75 cm from 625 cm, and 550 cm are left.

prompt.hi: Ab 550 cm ko metre aur cm mein badlo. Kitni dor bachi?
prompt.en: Now change 550 cm to metres and centimetres. How much string is left?

simpler.hi: 550 cm mein har 100 cm ek metre hai. Poore 100 gino, aur jo cm bachein unhe alag likho.
simpler.en: In 550 cm, every 100 cm is one metre. Count the full 100s, and write the cm left over separately.

why.hi: kul dor 625 cm thi, 75 cm lag gayi, toh 550 cm bachi, yaani 5 m 50 cm
why.en: the string was 625 cm in all, 75 cm got used, so 550 cm is left, that is 5 m 50 cm

answer.en: 5 m 50 cm of string is left

why.hi: kul dor 625 cm thi, 75 cm lag gayi, toh 550 cm bachi, yaani 5 m 50 cm
why.en: the string was 625 cm in all, 75 cm got used, so 550 cm is left, that is 5 m 50 cm

prompt.hi: Ek kamre ki deewar 4 m lambi hai. Deewar kitne cm lambi hai?
prompt.en: A wall of a room is 4 m long. How many cm long is the wall?

why.hi: deewar 4 m lambi hai, aur har 1 m mein 100 cm, toh 4 m = 400 cm
why.en: the wall is 4 m long, and each 1 m has 100 cm, so 4 m = 400 cm

simpler.hi: Har metre mein sau cm hote hain. Deewar 4 m hai, toh sau cm ko 4 baar jodo.
simpler.en: Each metre has a hundred cm. The wall is 4 m, so add a hundred cm 4 times.

prompt.hi: Ek rassi 2 m 7 cm lambi hai. Rassi kitne cm lambi hai?
prompt.en: A rope is 2 m 7 cm long. How many cm long is the rope?

why.hi: har 1 m = 100 cm, toh rassi ke 2 m = 200 cm, aur 200 + 7 = 207
why.en: each 1 m = 100 cm, so the rope's 2 m = 200 cm, and 200 + 7 = 207

simpler.hi: Pehle 2 m ko cm mein badlo, har metre sau cm. Phir usmein 7 cm jodo.
simpler.en: First change 2 m to cm, each metre is a hundred cm. Then add 7 cm to it.

prompt.hi: Ek ribbon 1 m 10 cm lamba hai, doosra ribbon 95 cm. Kaunsa lamba hai, pehla ya doosra?
prompt.en: One ribbon is 1 m 10 cm long, the other ribbon is 95 cm. Which is longer, the first or the second?

why.hi: doosra ribbon 95 cm hai, aur pehla 1 m 10 cm = 110 cm, jo zyada hai
why.en: the second ribbon is 95 cm, and the first is 1 m 10 cm = 110 cm, which is more

simpler.hi: Dono ko cm mein badlo: 1 m sau cm hota hai, usmein 10 cm aur jodo. Phir use 95 cm se milao.
simpler.en: Change both to cm: 1 m is a hundred cm, and add 10 cm more. Then compare it with 95 cm.

ladder.why: warm-up: 2 m → 200 cm, each metre is 100 cm
1 m plus 20 cm in a story → change the metre first → 120 cm
error spot: 1 m 5 cm written as 15 cm → it is 105 cm
the other way: 150 cm → 1 m 50 cm
compare 4 m 35 cm with 390 cm → change to one unit first

remediation.move: metre tape beside a 10 cm piece → the 10 cm piece is short → 10 such pieces fill the metre → 10 × 10 = 100 cm

say.hi: 10 cm toh metre scale ka ek chhota tukda hai. Aise 10 tukde milkar, yaani 10 × 10 = 100 cm, 1 m bante hain.
say.en: 10 cm is only a short piece of the metre scale. 10 such pieces together, that is 10 × 10 = 100 cm, make 1 m.

simpler.hi: 10 cm sirf ek chhota tukda hai. Aise 10 tukde jodo, tab 100 cm yaani 1 m banta hai.
simpler.en: 10 cm is just a short piece. Join 10 such pieces to make 100 cm, that is 1 m.

prompt.hi: Ek rassi 5 m lambi hai. Woh kitne cm lambi hai?
prompt.en: A rope is 5 m long. How many cm long is it?

why.hi: rassi 5 m lambi hai, aur har 1 m mein 100 cm, toh 5 m = 500 cm
why.en: the rope is 5 m long, and each 1 m has 100 cm, so 5 m = 500 cm

simpler.hi: Har metre mein sau cm hote hain. Rassi 5 m hai, toh sau cm ko 5 baar jodo.
simpler.en: Each metre has a hundred cm. The rope is 5 m, so add a hundred cm 5 times.

remediation.move: place-value chart where the metre fills the hundreds place: 1 m 5 cm → 100 + 5 → 105; joining the digits as 15 drops the hundred

say.hi: Pehle metre ko cm banao, phir bache hue cm jodo. 1 m 5 cm = 100 + 5 = 105 cm, 15 cm nahi.
say.en: First change the metre to cm, then add the extra cm. 1 m 5 cm = 100 + 5 = 105 cm, not 15 cm.

simpler.hi: 1 m matlab 100 cm. Usme 5 cm aur jodo, toh 105 cm hota hai.
simpler.en: 1 m is 100 cm. Add the extra 5 cm and you get 105 cm.

prompt.hi: Ek dupatta 2 m 9 cm lamba hai. Woh kitne cm lamba hai?
prompt.en: A dupatta is 2 m 9 cm long. How many cm long is it?

why.hi: 1 m = 100 cm, toh dupatta ke 2 m = 200 cm, aur 200 + 9 = 209
why.en: 1 m = 100 cm, so the dupatta's 2 m = 200 cm, and 200 + 9 = 209

simpler.hi: Pehle 2 m ko cm mein badlo, har metre sau cm. Phir usmein 9 cm jodo.
simpler.en: First change 2 m to cm, each metre is a hundred cm. Then add 9 cm to it.

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab hum cm aur m dono jaante hain. Agla sawaal yeh hai ki kis cheez ke liye cm theek hai aur kis ke liye m. Ab andaaza lagana seekhenge.
bridgeToNext.en: Now we know both cm and m. The next question is which things suit cm and which suit m. Next we learn to estimate.

simpler.hi: Ab cm aur m dono aate hain. Agle hisse mein andaaza lagayenge ki kis cheez ke liye cm theek hai aur kis ke liye m.
simpler.en: Now you know both cm and m. Next we estimate which things suit cm and which suit m.

hook.convey: benchmarks: 1 cm ≈ a fingertip's width, 1 m ≈ one big step of an adult; small things in cm, big things in m; a number means nothing without its unit, so compare lengths only in one unit

use.hi: Cricket ki pitch bahut lambi hoti hai, aur wicket usse kaafi chhote. Dono ki lambai alag ikai mein batate hain. Aaj sahi ikai chunna seekhenge.
use.en: A cricket pitch is very long, and the wickets are much shorter. Their lengths are told in different units. Today we learn to choose the right unit.

use.hi: Billi ki poonchh aur haathi ki oonchai, dono ek hi ikai mein naapna theek nahi lagta. Billi ki poonchh cm mein aur haathi m mein. Aaj dekhenge kyun.
use.en: A cat's tail and an elephant's height do not suit the same unit. The cat's tail goes in cm and the elephant in m. Today we see why.

explain.convey: benchmarks: 1 cm ≈ the width of a fingertip, 1 m ≈ one big step of an adult → small things in cm, big things in m

point.hi: 1 cm lagbhag tumhari ungli ki chaudai jitna hai, ungli jitna. 1 m lagbhag ek bade aadmi ka ek bada kadam hai. Chhoti cheezein cm mein naapte hain, badi cheezein m mein.
point.en: 1 cm is about the width of your fingertip, about a fingertip. 1 m is about one big step of a grown-up. Small things are measured in cm, big things in m.

prompt.hi: Ek rubber lagbhag 4 ungliyon jitna lamba hai. Uski lambai ke liye kaunsa theek hai, 4 cm ya 4 m?
prompt.en: An eraser is about as long as 4 fingertips. Which suits its length, 4 cm or 4 m?

why.hi: 1 cm ek ungli jitna hai, toh 4 ungliyan lagbhag 4 cm; 1 m toh ek bada kadam hai
why.en: 1 cm is about one finger wide, so 4 fingers are about 4 cm; 1 m is a big step

simpler.hi: 1 cm lagbhag ek ungli ki chaudai hai, aur 1 m ek bada kadam. Rubber chhoti cheez hai, toh woh chhoti unit mein naapa jaata hai.
simpler.en: 1 cm is about one fingertip wide, and 1 m is one big step. An eraser is a small thing, so it is measured in the small unit.

explain.convey: a cricket pitch is about 20 m long and 3 m wide → about 20 big steps; 20 cm would be a little more than a pencil

point.hi: Cricket ki pitch lagbhag 20 m lambi aur 3 m chaudi hoti hai, yaani lagbhag 20 bade kadam. Agar koi 20 cm likhe, toh woh bas ek pencil se thoda bada hoga.
point.en: A cricket pitch is about 20 m long and 3 m wide, that is about 20 big steps. If someone wrote 20 cm, it would be just a little longer than a pencil.

prompt.hi: Isi pitch ke dono sire pe wicket lagte hain. Wicket ki oonchai lagbhag kitni hogi, 70 cm ya 70 m?
prompt.en: Wickets stand at both ends of this pitch. About how tall is a wicket, 70 cm or 70 m?

why.hi: 70 m toh poori 20 m ki pitch se bhi lamba hoga, wicket itna ooncha nahi hota
why.en: 70 m would be longer than the whole 20 m pitch; a wicket is not that tall

simpler.hi: Poori pitch hi 20 m lambi hai. Wicket pitch se bahut chhota hota hai, toh socho kaunsi unit theek baithti hai.
simpler.en: The whole pitch is only 20 m long. A wicket is much shorter than the pitch, so think which unit fits.

explain.convey: 30 cm ruler vs 1 m stick: 30 is the bigger number but the units differ → 1 m = 100 cm → 100 cm > 30 cm → change to one unit, then compare

point.hi: 30 bada number hai aur 1 chhota, par dono ki ikai alag hai. 1 m = 100 cm, toh 1 m ka danda 100 cm ka hai, 30 cm ke scale se lamba. Pehle dono ko ek hi ikai mein badlo, phir tulna karo.
point.en: 30 is a bigger number and 1 is smaller, but their units are different. 1 m = 100 cm, so the 1 m stick is 100 cm, longer than the 30 cm ruler. First change both to one unit, then compare.

prompt.hi: Ek rassi 150 cm ki hai, doosri rassi 2 m ki. Kaunsi lambi hai, 150 cm wali ya 2 m wali?
prompt.en: One rope is 150 cm, the other rope is 2 m. Which is longer, the 150 cm one or the 2 m one?

why.hi: doosri rassi 2 m = 200 cm hai, jo pehli rassi ke 150 cm se zyada hai
why.en: the second rope is 2 m = 200 cm, more than the first rope's 150 cm

simpler.hi: Pehle dono ko ek unit mein badlo: 1 m = 100 cm. Toh 2 m ko cm mein badlo, phir 150 cm se milao.
simpler.en: First change both to one unit: 1 m = 100 cm. So change 2 m to cm, then compare with 150 cm.

problem.hi: Har cheez ke liye sahi andaaza chuno. School bus ki lambai 10 cm hai ya 10 m? Nayi pencil 15 cm hai ya 15 m? School desk lagbhag 1 m hai ya 10 m?
problem.en: Choose the sensible estimate for each. Is a school bus 10 cm or 10 m long? Is a new pencil 15 cm or 15 m? Is a school desk about 1 m or 10 m?

simpler.hi: Ungli ki chaudai lagbhag 1 cm hai, aur ek bada kadam lagbhag 1 m. Pehle sirf bus ke baare mein socho: woh 10 ungli jitni lambi hai ya 10 kadam jitni.
simpler.en: A fingertip is about 1 cm wide, and one big step is about 1 m. First think only about the bus: is it as long as 10 fingertips or as 10 steps.

givens.hi: 1 cm lagbhag ek ungli ki chaudai hai
givens.en: 1 cm ≈ the width of a fingertip

givens.hi: 1 m lagbhag ek bada kadam hai

find.hi: bus, pencil aur desk ke liye sahi andaaza
find.en: the sensible estimate for the bus, the pencil and the desk

do.hi: Pehle bus ko bade kadam se socho
do.en: First think of the bus in big steps

steps.result: bus lagbhag 10 bade kadam lambi, toh 10 m

why.hi: har bada kadam lagbhag 1 m hota hai, isliye 10 bade kadam lagbhag 10 m hain
why.en: each big step is about 1 m, so 10 big steps are about 10 m

simpler.hi: Ek bada kadam lagbhag 1 m hai. Bus lagbhag 10 bade kadam lambi hai, toh woh 10 m hai.
simpler.en: One big step is about 1 m. The bus is about 10 big steps long, so it is 10 m.

do.hi: Ab pencil ko ungli ki chaudai se milao
do.en: Now match the pencil with fingertip widths

steps.result: pencil lagbhag 15 ungliyon jitni, toh 15 cm

why.hi: har ungli ki chaudai lagbhag 1 cm hoti hai, isliye 15 ungliyon jitni lambai lagbhag 15 cm hai
why.en: each fingertip width is about 1 cm, so a length of 15 fingertips is about 15 cm

simpler.hi: Ek ungli ki chaudai lagbhag 1 cm hai. Pencil lagbhag 15 ungliyon jitni hai, toh 15 cm.
simpler.en: One fingertip is about 1 cm wide. The pencil is about 15 fingertips long, so 15 cm.

prompt.hi: Ab desk ki baari. Desk lagbhag ek bada kadam hai ya 10 bade kadam? Toh desk lagbhag 1 m hai ya 10 m?
prompt.en: Now the desk. Is the desk about one big step or 10 big steps? So is the desk about 1 m or 10 m?

simpler.hi: Desk ke saath ek bada kadam rakh kar socho. Desk lagbhag jitne kadam lamba hai, utne hi metre hai.
simpler.en: Imagine one big step beside the desk. The desk is as many metres long as the big steps it takes.

why.hi: desk lagbhag ek bada kadam hai, toh 1 m, jaise bus 10 m aur pencil 15 cm
why.en: the desk is about one big step, so 1 m, just as the bus is 10 m and the pencil 15 cm

answer.hi: bus 10 m, pencil 15 cm, aur desk lagbhag 1 m
answer.en: bus 10 m, pencil 15 cm, and desk about 1 m

why.hi: desk lagbhag ek bada kadam hai, toh 1 m, jaise bus 10 m aur pencil 15 cm
why.en: the desk is about one big step, so 1 m, just as the bus is 10 m and the pencil 15 cm

prompt.hi: Ek kitaab 25 cm lambi hai aur ek palang 2 m lamba. Kaun zyada lamba hai, kitaab ya palang?
prompt.en: A book is 25 cm long and a bed is 2 m long. Which is longer, the book or the bed?

why.hi: palang 2 m = 200 cm hai, jo kitaab ke 25 cm se zyada hai
why.en: the bed is 2 m = 200 cm, more than the book's 25 cm

simpler.hi: Pehle dono ko cm mein badlo, har metre sau cm. 2 m ko cm mein badal kar 25 cm se milao.
simpler.en: First change both to cm, each metre is a hundred cm. Change 2 m to cm and compare it with 25 cm.

prompt.hi: {friend} ne likha ki ek kamre ki lambai 6 cm hai. Kya yeh andaaza theek hai, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: {friend} wrote that a room is 6 cm long. Is this estimate sensible, yes or no?

why.hi: 6 cm sirf 6 ungliyon jitna hai, aur kamra usse bahut lamba hota hai, toh yeh andaaza theek nahi
why.en: 6 cm is only as long as 6 fingers, and a room is far longer, so this estimate is not right

simpler.hi: 6 cm sirf 6 ungliyon jitna hota hai. Ab socho, kamra itna chhota ho sakta hai ya nahi.
simpler.en: 6 cm is only as long as 6 fingertips. Now think whether a room can be that small.

prompt.hi: Ek seedhi 3 m lambi hai aur ek rassi 250 cm lambi. Kaun zyada lamba hai, seedhi ya rassi?
prompt.en: A ladder is 3 m long and a rope is 250 cm long. Which is longer, the ladder or the rope?

why.hi: 3 m = 300 cm, jo 250 cm se zyada hai
why.en: 3 m = 300 cm, which is more than 250 cm

simpler.hi: Pehle dono ko cm mein badlo, har metre sau cm. 3 m ko cm mein badal kar 250 cm se milao.
simpler.en: First change both to cm, each metre is a hundred cm. Change 3 m to cm and compare it with 250 cm.

ladder.why: warm-up estimate: a door is about 2 m, not 2 cm
80 cm vs 1 m → change to one unit, the 1 m rope is longer
judge an estimate: a corridor is 25 m, not 25 cm

remediation.move: metre tape stood against a door with a 15 cm pencil at its foot → 15 vs 2 → change to one unit: 2 m = 200 cm → 15 cm vs 200 cm → the door is far longer; a number means nothing without its unit

say.hi: Sirf number mat dekho, ikai bhi dekho. 2 m = 200 cm hai, toh 2 m ka darwaza 15 cm ki pencil se bahut lamba hai.
say.en: Do not look only at the number; look at the unit too. 2 m = 200 cm, so a 2 m door is much longer than a 15 cm pencil.

simpler.hi: Number ke saath ikai bhi dekho. 2 m matlab 200 cm, jo 15 cm se bahut lamba hai.
simpler.en: Look at the unit as well as the number. 2 m is 200 cm, much longer than 15 cm.

prompt.hi: Ek mez 1 m lambi hai aur ek kitaab 40 cm. Kaun zyada lamba hai, mez ya kitaab?
prompt.en: A table is 1 m long and a book is 40 cm. Which is longer, the table or the book?

why.hi: mez 1 m = 100 cm hai, jo kitaab ke 40 cm se zyada hai
why.en: the table is 1 m = 100 cm, more than the book's 40 cm

simpler.hi: 1 m sau cm ke barabar hai. Ise 40 cm se milao, jo zyada ho woh lamba hai.
simpler.en: 1 m equals a hundred cm. Compare that with 40 cm; the bigger one is longer.
